status_definitions.NORMATIVE: A proposed value or governing choice; empirical work can challenge consequences without settling the value.
status_definitions.INSPECTED: A bounded observation of source material, not independent validation.
status_definitions.LITERATURE_OBSERVATION: A limited paraphrase of identified primary sources within their declared scope.
status_definitions.PROPOSED: A specified design or study that has not been implemented or run here.
status_definitions.HYPOTHESIS: An outcome claim to test against named alternatives.
status_definitions.DERIVED: An elementary conditional argument supplied in the paper, not a novelty finding or production proof.

claims.statement: The proposed goal is useful intelligence that expands human choice and capability alongside reliable controls.
claims.boundary: Goal choice, not an experimentally established condition.
claims.challenge: Assess practical value and tradeoffs with the people affected; no task-performance score alone settles the value.

claims.statement: Inspected Framework and selected later recovered sources motivate the strands; the public frontier report preserves a same-information generic tie. Their stronger interpretations remain bounded by source status.
claims.boundary: Selected provenance and source interpretation, not independent validation. Recovered publication clearance remains unresolved; private archives stay outside this repository.
claims.challenge: A source mapping unsupported by its inspected passages must be corrected.

claims.statement: The selected primary literature supplies the limited observations described in section 3.
claims.boundary: Statements are restricted to those source scopes; no empirical result is transferred to this Framework.
claims.challenge: Check each cited statement against the stated source revision and inspection depth; broader claims require more literature.

claims.statement: A six-dimension practical-control profile is a candidate alternative to prematurely combining sovereignty into one score.
claims.boundary: No validated construct, scale, thresholds or universal definition of freedom.
claims.challenge: Usability and construct-validity work may show missing dimensions, poor discrimination or harmful tradeoffs.

claims.statement: Separate record kinds, use states and derivative invalidation may make personal representation more correctable.
claims.boundary: Conceptual lifecycle; no schema, dependency-completeness proof, deletion implementation or machine-unlearning result.
claims.challenge: Study A: prohibited reuse, failed visible repair or unacceptable loss of useful retrieval challenges the specified mechanism.

claims.statement: Identical complete surviving reconstruction inputs cannot guarantee exact decoding of two histories that differ in a withdrawn payload.
claims.boundary: Elementary argument conditional on identical complete input and no distinguishing side information; no novelty claim.
claims.challenge: Locate a valid decoder satisfying those assumptions that reconstructs both histories exactly, or identify an assumption not met in a proposed application.

claims.statement: Source-aware, reasoned disagreement may improve collective judgement over simpler alternatives at matched resources.
claims.boundary: No independence, performance or consciousness guarantee. Roles are not independently observed sources.
claims.challenge: Study C: no worthwhile improvement, excessive false objections or an unacceptable completion/cost loss rejects the specified performance claim.

claims.statement: Strict requirements a and not-a for the same exclusive decision have no jointly satisfying outcome.
claims.boundary: Set-intersection argument; it does not choose legitimate authority or a universal social conflict policy.
claims.challenge: A purported satisfying outcome must actually meet both exclusive requirements under the stated decision model.

claims.statement: Conditioning on a known deterministic duplicate E' adds no information beyond E: P(H|E,E')=P(H|E), where defined.
claims.boundary: No novelty or calibrated source-independence claim; additional observations and hidden dependencies require a different model.
claims.challenge: Exhibit additional information or a non-deterministic relation and the duplicate assumption no longer applies; otherwise the conditioning identity must hold.

claims.statement: An interactive companion and authored world may support worthwhile work and learning, compared with simpler presentations.
claims.boundary: Product expression only; no implementation, participant learning, retention or engagement result.
claims.challenge: R05: compare delayed unassisted/transfer tasks, effort and access; more time spent alone cannot establish learning.

claims.statement: Affected-party standing, community control and legitimate conflict procedures belong in the governance specification.
claims.boundary: Proposed terms requiring actual partner authority; no community representation, endorsement or legal claim.
claims.challenge: Affected partners may reject the terms; observed procedure quality and decision influence can challenge the mechanism, not decide values for everyone.

claims.statement: Operational trust and possible welfare concern require different arguments; compliance is not a decisive moral-status test.
claims.boundary: Explicit challenge to a reading of the historical rights chapter; no diagnosis of current models or settled consciousness criterion.
claims.challenge: Review the distinctions under competing moral theories and welfare evidence; conduct changes alone cannot settle the premise about morally significant interests.

claims.statement: Eight connected research tracks and studies A-C define candidate comparisons and outcomes, with none yet run.
claims.boundary: Not a preregistration, sample-size calculation, funded programme, execution board or empirical result.
claims.challenge: Before confirmatory work freeze population, measures, worthwhile effects, sample rationale and stop conditions; accept failure on declared comparisons.

claims.statement: The earlier inspected simulator revision exposed accounting and freshness limits. The later self-authored repair report addresses accounting within one live authority while freshness remains open; none of this validates the AI-futures proposals.
claims.boundary: Pinned earlier packet sources and the later bounded simulator repair report; no model-agent, memory, learning or production validation.
claims.challenge: Check the previous receipt and raw reproducer; changing these limits requires a separate implementation and verification.
